newsitem.title: UK: Salehurst to float on May 6, eyes growth prospects.
newsitem.headline: Salehurst to float on May 6, eyes growth prospects.

text.p: Specialist paper distributor Salehurst Plc said on Tuesday it is planning to float on the London Stock Exchange on May 6 and will use the proceeds to cut debts and take advantage of growth opportunities.
The company said it has raised about two million stg of new money, net of expenses, following a four million stg placing at 117p.
The market capitlisation of Salehurst will be approximately 15.5 million stg based on the issue price.

The balance of the placing was made up by shares sold by Michael Jackson, the chief executive and majority shareholder, who, with his family, will retain an approximate 65 per cent holding in the company.
Salehurst purchases and supplies paper primarily to magazine publishers. It also provides its customers with related stock management, technical, advisory and computer information services.

The company said it differs from competitors, such as paper mill agents and paper merchants, by offering value added services including independent advice on the quality, pricing and usage of different types of paper.
Salehurst made a pre-tax profit of 974,000 stg for the full year ended January 31 1997, up from 863,000 stg in the previous year.
Jackson said that profits for the first two months of the current year were ahead of the company's budget although he declined to give a profit forecast.
He added that the tonnage of paper delivered for the two month period was "significantly up on last year."

Commenting on Salehurst's growth prospects, Jackson said: "The industry in the UK has gone through a process of demerging and we may make an acquisition if it is a complimentary fit. But for the moment we have nothing in mind."
